newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P puts Atlas Copco on creditwatch.
newsitem.headline: S&P puts Atlas Copco on creditwatch.

text.p: U.S. credit rating agency Standard & Poor's (S&P) said on Monday that it had placed Swedish industrial engineer Atlas Copco on creditwatch with a negative outlook.
S&P said the move followed the announcement of a cash tender offer for the U.S. equipment leasing company Prime Service Inc made earlier on Monday.

"The debt financed acquisition will, if realised, increase Atlas Copco's leverage and raise net debt to capital to about 35 percent to 40 percent (from being cash positive) on a pro forma basis," S&P said in a statement.
"The acquisition will change Atlas Copco's business mix somewhat and the impact on the business risk needs to be further explored."
The engineer currently has an A-1 corporate credit rating.
Atlas Copco said the offer will start on June 9 and be open for 20 business days.
"S&P will review Atlas Copco's credit quality based on the new operating and financial strategies upon the completion of the acquisition," the agency said.
At 1110 GMT Atlas Copco shares were two crowns higher at 211.5 crowns.
